items: Raw sprouts – Don't eat them uncooked if you're pregnant or immunocompromised (warm, humid growing conditions make them a common Salmonella source)
Garlic in oil – Don't store homemade garlic-oil at room temperature (low-oxygen environment can let Clostridium botulinum grow)
Eggs – Don't store them on the fridge door (temperature swings there speed up bacterial growth through the shell)
Ground meat – Don't thaw it on the counter (outer layer sits in the bacteria danger zone long before the center defrosts)
Soft cheeses – Don't store them next to ready-to-eat foods without wrapping (Listeria can transfer easily in the fridge)
Leftover rice-based dishes – Don't cool them slowly on the stove (bacteria multiply fastest in the first hours after cooking)
Almonds are technically not nuts at all
